title: Trump Gives Green Light to U.S. Companies to Aim Hacks at Cybercriminals
summary: The practice would align the United States more closely with countries like China and Russia, where spy agencies have long relied on private-sector hackers to help with national security missions.

title: U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln Has Been Deployed for Months, Prompting Concerns
summary: The U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln has been deployed for nearly nine months. Members of Congress are worried about the crew’s well-being.

title: American Missionary Kidnapped in Niger Is Said to Be Released From Captivity
summary: The release of Kevin Rideout, an American missionary pilot who was seized in Niger’s capital last fall, has been a priority for the White House.

title: Judge Dismisses Trump Administration’s Antisemitism Case Against Harvard
summary: The government argued the university had not done enough to combat antisemitism during campus protests. A judge called the incidents “isolated and episodic.”

title: Deaths of 3 ICE Detainees Prompt Questions About Medical Care
summary: Immigrants at Delaney Hall in Newark have complained about health services. Federal officials defended the treatment provided there and elsewhere.

title: Appeals Court Sidesteps Key Question Over Trump’s Use of Alien Enemies Act
summary: The court dismissed a case over the Alien Enemies Act in a messy conclusion to a long-running legal battle that had seemed destined to end up before the Supreme Court.

title: Trump’s Immigration Policy Echoes 1920s Crackdown, but This Time Congress Isn’t Involved
summary: U.S. leaders limited immigration amid economic and social turmoil. Historians see similarities to Trump’s crackdown, with a catch: He’s doing it without Congress.

title: Farage Wins Special U.K. Election That He Initiated, as Expected
summary: Nigel Farage, the leader of Reform U.K., won the Clacton by-election with 63 percent. Count Binface, his costumed main rival, came second with 27 percent, a personal best.

title: Afghan Women Erased From Public Life in Five Years of Taliban Rule
summary: Decrees restricting the rights of women and girls to study, work, travel and act independently now threaten to damage Afghanistan permanently, experts say.

title: The Golden Age of Mexican Food Is Here. And It’s Complicated.
summary: Even at a time of anti-immigration politics, there has never been a richer variety of Mexican restaurants in the United States.

title: 41 of the Greatest Mexican Restaurants In the United States
summary: Our favorite choices for seafood from Sonora, carnitas from Michoacán, chalupas from Puebla and so much more.

title: What to Know About Luigi Mangione’s Court Cases and Potential Plea Deal
summary: Mr. Mangione faces federal charges of stalking that resulted in the death of a health insurance executive. A guilty plea could close the federal case — and complicate a separate state murder trial.

title: California May Let Residents Choose ‘Jewish’ as an Ethnic Identifier
summary: A bill would allow Jews to identify themselves as an ethnic group on state forms. Supporters argue it’s a step toward acknowledging the complex nature of Jewish identity.

title: A City Mobilizes Against a Stubborn Health Threat: Mosquitoes
summary: The city of Belém in northern Brazil was overwhelmed by an outbreak of dengue two years ago. An all-out municipal effort has reduced cases and may offer lessons to American cities.

title: How a Long-Shot U.S. Oil Drilling Project Is Shaking Up Greenland
summary: A U.S. oil company says it could be on the verge of a major discovery in Greenland. The proposal comes at a tricky time for the Arctic island, and locals are lining up against it.

title: Israeli Settlers Resume West Bank Siege After Eviction
summary: The military’s failure to keep extremists away from two Palestinian families trapped in their West Bank homes made clear the chaos gripping the Israeli-occupied territory.

title: Charlie Kirk Suspect Fights Death Penalty, Says No Others Were in Danger
summary: Prosecutors say they can seek the death penalty against Tyler Robinson because he also endangered people near Charlie Kirk, who was shot in the throat last year. Mr. Robinson’s lawyers note that the gunman struck only his target.

title: Outdated American Policy Is Hurting the Afghan People
summary: A new generation of Afghans wants to move on from the animosities of the past, but Western policies make that difficult.

title: Hamas Has No More Cards to Play
summary: The signs point to Hamas being serious about disarming. The recent Board of Peace plan for it to surrender its weapons should be carried out.

title: Jimmy Fallon Reacts to Karoline Leavitt’s White House Exit
summary: The “Tonight Show” host said President Trump had been surprised by the press secretary’s decision to step down. “She was like, ‘I wanted to wait for a good time but there hasn’t been one, so.’”

title: Engine Blade Hit Window on Jet Before Man Was Partly Sucked Outside, Report Says
summary: The National Transportation Safety Board said it had found a bird’s remains and feathers on a broken engine.
